chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Salih said:

They wanted to sell the dates of the spring of Abu Ziyad, so I wanted to buy them, then I said, 'Until I ask for permission from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).' So I sent a messenger to ask him, and he said, 'Tell him to buy it; if he does not buy it, someone else will buy it.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (title of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq)
key_terms.عَيْنٍ: Spring (source of water, here referring to a date garden watered by a specific spring)
key_terms.مُصَادِفاً: A messenger or envoy sent to convey a message

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying dates from a specific tree or spring before harvest in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Jamil ibn Salih highlights the practical application of *gharar* (uncertainty) in pre-harvest produce sales, where the Imam’s permission validates the transaction despite the produce not yet being fully separated. The Imam’s directive—'let him buy it; if he does not, someone else will'—underscores the flexibility of Shia commercial jurisprudence, prioritizing the validity of the contract over rigid conditions, provided the core elements of sale are met. This reflects the broader Shia scholarly view that moderate uncertainty in agricultural goods is permissible when the seller has possession and the price is known.
